card: Enables the -Wmissing-noreturn compiler warning flag in CMake and adds missing [[noreturn]] attributes to functions, methods, and lambdas that unconditionally throw or abort. It also qualifies bare exit, abort, and _Exit calls with the std namespace, and adds warning-suppression pragmas for fuzzing initialization code that conditionally exits depending on the build configuration. This eliminates compiler static analysis false positives across different compiler versions and prevents future omissions of the attribute.
changed_since_previous: No substantial changes to the approach or scope since the previous review.
evidence: PR description: "Missing `[[noreturn]]` attributes can cause compiler false positives and other issues; see discussion in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35896#discussion_r3726612556."
PR description: "Some `[[noreturn]]` additions may appear redundant, however they suppress warnings for various compiler versions..."
problem: Functions that terminate or unconditionally throw without `[[noreturn]]` attributes can cause compiler diagnostics and static analysis to produce false positives (such as unreachable code warnings or missing return statements). In addition, without compiler enforcement, missing annotations are easily reintroduced.

risk.why: Incorrectly marking a function as non-returning would cause undefined behavior if it actually returned, but all annotated functions unconditionally throw or exit.

scope_notes: A mechanical cleanup touching multiple subsystems to add annotations, qualify standard library functions with `std::`, and enable a compiler warning flag.
summary: Enables the `-Wmissing-noreturn` compiler warning flag in the build system and annotates non-returning functions, methods, and lambdas across the codebase with `[[noreturn]]`. It also prefixes standard exit and termination calls with `std::` (`std::exit`, `std::abort`, `std::_Exit`), and adds compiler pragmas to silence warnings in fuzzing setup code whose return behavior depends on the build configuration.
